subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden mixed trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` suppression, and what boundary should separate silent-intent internal text from legitimate substantive replies that append or mention the token?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve some mixed trailing-token replies, while the issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; choosing that boundary affects both security and message-loss behavior.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal/status preambles and reasoning-like silent intent while preserving legitimate substantive replies, then update all delivery paths to use it.

options.title: Use blanket trailing-token suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` token and accept that some currently visible replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-only, reasoning-prefixed, and scoped cron cases are suppressed, and close broader mixed-content suppression as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal/status preambles and reasoning-like silent intent while preserving legitimate substantive replies, then update all delivery paths to use it.
